name: Neru Fragment
summary: The Neru Fragment is one of four ancient carved stone pieces belonging to the Goaz Stone, a relic discovered in the Whelgar's Excavation site within the Wetlands. Unearthed from the disturbed earth, it holds a segment of ancient Titan script detailing the primeval history of Azeroth.

sections.title: Piece of the Goaz Stone
sections.body: Discovered by the dwarven archaeological expedition led by Prospector Whelgar, the Goaz Stone broke apart into four distinct remnants: the Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru fragments. When raptors overrun the dig site, work ground to a halt, leaving the Neru Fragment buried beneath loose soil amid the aggressive beasts. Recovering this fragment is crucial for reassembling the tablet, allowing dwarven scholars to decipher a forgotten record whose surviving words mention a divine plan and a doomed prophecy.

sections.title: Reading the Restored Tablet
sections.body: Once the four fragments restore the Goaz Stone, Prospector Whelgar continues translating its Titan script. The newly legible words speak of Old Gods chained beneath the land.

faq.answer: It is an ancient stone piece broken off from a larger relic called the Goaz Stone. It was uncovered by the dwarven expedition in the Wetlands before raptors overran their dig.
It lies scattered in the raptor-infested Whelgar's Excavation in the southern Wetlands, typically buried under loose soil or hidden among abandoned artifacts.

faq.q: What happens when all four fragments are gathered?
aliases: what does the goaz stone say
faq.answer: Prospector Whelgar pieces the Goaz Stone back together so he can continue translating its Titan script and investigate the mystery hinted at by its surviving text.

angles.text: For the Explorer's League, recovering tablet pieces like the Neru Fragment is vital to unearthing Titan secrets and piecing together the origins of dwarven kind.
